intended_object: An intermediate field S of a field extension E/F is finitely generated over F: S = F(t) for some finite subset t ⊆ E. Taken from the docstring and the Stacks tag 09FZ.
explanation: The definition says S is finitely generated exactly when some finite set t of elements of E satisfies `adjoin F t = S`, where `adjoin` gives the intermediate field generated by t. This is the textbook meaning of a finitely generated subextension. It works the same way as `Subalgebra.FG` and `Submodule.FG`, which use a `Finset` of generators. No elements of S are lost by taking the generators from E: if adjoin F t = S, then t ⊆ S. Degenerate cases also come out right: S = ⊥ is generated by t = ∅. The setting of fields and intermediate fields is the natural one for this notion. The algebra version, `Subalgebra.FG`, is a different notion, since a field can be finitely generated as a field without being finitely generated as an algebra. So this is not a narrower copy of an existing Mathlib definition.
